issues.detail: The Greek 'αναστας' (anastas) is a participle modifying the subject who gives (the friend), meaning 'arising' or 'getting up'. The Vietnamese translation 'dầu người ấy không dậy mà cho' suggests a conditional 'even if he doesn't get up to give', whereas the Greek structure 'ει και ου δωσει αυτω αναστας... εγερθεις δωσει' is a rhetorical contrast: 'even if he does not give to him [while] arising... [but] because of his shamelessness, [having been] aroused, he will give him'.
